# H6 — Protocol surface completion: MCP Streamable HTTP + cross-process trace

**Mission** — Give the kit's MCP surface a remote lane and give traces process-crossing legs. Done looks like: `kits/mcp-server` serves its existing tool surface over a single-POST Streamable HTTP endpoint (stateless, bounded, fail-closed) with byte-identical dispatch semantics to stdio; `foundations/agent/mcp-client` can consume a remote server over the same transport; and one `TraceContext` RunID survives an agent → subprocess → MCP-over-HTTP → tool-call chain, stamped onto every telemetry event on both sides. This serves the north star — "every claim checked against ground truth" — because a claim about a multi-process run is only checkable when its evidence correlates into one trace, and because the HTTP transport is absorbed from a consumer-proven pattern (fathom's hand-rolled `serve-http`), not invented speculatively.

**Repos & write scope** — Writes ONLY to `/Volumes/m2ext/code/geoffmilleraz/agentic-kit`. `../sextant`, `../throughline`, `../growing-gardens-bi` are READ-ONLY grounding (sextant-side donor adoption is H4's job, gated on its branch merging).

**Trigger** — Stage A/C (trace, roadmap #21): FIRED. `docs/roadmap.md` #21 subscribes on "the first multi-process agent topology"; that topology exists — `foundations/agent/mcp-client/doc.go` documents the boundedexec→subprocess-server composition as the intended shape, and the fleet runs one daily (`../sextant/cmd/fathom/servehttp.go`, an MCP daemon queried cross-process by editor sessions). Stage B (HTTP server, roadmap #15 transport half): FIRED via pull doctrine. #15 subscribes on "an MCP server must serve non-local clients"; the concrete subscriber is **fathom `serve-http`** — a hand-rolled JSON-RPC-over-HTTP MCP endpoint (`newHTTPHandler`, `POST /rpc`, 4 MB `http.MaxBytesReader`, own `internal/mcp` dispatch) already in production at `../sextant/cmd/fathom/servehttp.go`. The kit absorbs the proven pattern; fathom deleting its copy is H4 hand-off, not this spec. The prompts/resources half of #15 has NOT fired — no server has content to serve. Re-verify all three quotes by reading the named files before building.

## Current state (grounding)

- `docs/designs/mcp-streamable-http.md` is the design record: single POST endpoint, JSON or SSE response content-type, **stateless first implementation** (no `mcp-session-id`), SSE/keepalive/notifications explicitly deferred, W3C `traceparent` mapping (`RunID`→trace-id, `SpanID`→parent-id, flags `01`), ≈20 lines per side, no OTel.
- `kits/mcp-server` (stdio-only today): `Serve(ctx, in, out)` owns bufio framing/resync (`server.go:73`); the transport-agnostic core is `(*Server).dispatch(ctx, req) (any, *rpcError, callMeta)` (`handlers.go:24`) and `(*Server).serveReq` (`server.go:194`, call-log dance). `knownProtocolVersions` (map[string]bool, `types.go:42-47`) includes `"2025-11-25"` (line 46); `latestProtocolVersion = "2025-11-25"` (`types.go:51`). Server keeps NO handshake state and does not enforce initialize-before-use (`doc.go` §JSON-RPC correctness) — already stateless-ready. `doc.go` says "Transport is stdio ONLY" and names the streamable-HTTP roadmap. `schema.cue` + `testdata/` exist. Notifications (`isNotification`) get no response; batches rejected -32600; oversized → -32700 + `bestEffortID`, fail-closed resync.
- `foundations/agent/mcp-client`: `Transport` interface `{Send, Receive, Close}` (`transport.go:26`); `NewIOTransport` is the only impl; `DefaultMaxMessageBytes = 4<<20` matching the kit. `Client.New` does initialize handshake (`offeredVersions = {"2025-11-25","2025-06-18"}`, `client.go:17`), pins tool-description hashes (SHA-256, `ToolChangedError`, `Repin`), `CallTool`/`ListTools`; `bridge.go` `RegisterAll` feeds tool-registry. Client serializes each send→receive under `c.mu`.
- `foundations/telemetry/event/trace.go`: `TraceContext{RunID, SpanID, ParentSpanID}`, `WithTrace`/`TraceFrom`/`Apply`/`NewTrace`/`Child`; ID widths already W3C-aligned (16-byte run, 8-byte span, hex); injectable `randHex(nBytes int) string`. **No traceparent codec exists anywhere** (`grep -rn traceparent --include='*.go' .` → zero hits). The package's existing `schema.cue` is unaffected — trace.go's file comment already notes reserved attrs don't touch the open `#Attributes` map, and the codec adds no new data shape.
- `foundations/agent/bounded-exec`: `Config.Env []string` is the COMPLETE child env, never inherited (`types.go:86-91`); tests use real subprocesses, skip without `/bin/sh` (documented determinism deviation).
- Trace producers ready to correlate: `kits/agent-harness/harness.go` auto-roots a trace (`event.WithTrace(ctx, event.NewTrace(nil))`) at every entrypoint (lines 200, 241, 276, 349, 419, 448, 598; stamps at 1184); `foundations/llmclient/instrument/telemetry.go:151` stamps `TraceFrom` onto LLM-call events.
- Spec-revision check (done 2026-07-15, externally re-verified): the MCP **2026-07-28 RC** makes the protocol core stateless and removes the initialize/initialized handshake and `Mcp-Session-Id`; final ships 2026-07-28 ([RC announcement](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28-release-candidate/), [2025-11-25 spec](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25)). The design note's stateless direction is confirmed. Do NOT bump `latestProtocolVersion` past 2025-11-25 until the final revision publishes.
- `TRACKING.md` deferred list carries `[-] HTTP MCP transport — … design note: docs/designs/mcp-streamable-http.md`. Pull queue has open rows (D35-3/4/5) — this spec is exempt from the doctrine block only because every stage is itself consumer-proven/triggered work, not a zero-consumer package; record that reasoning in the TRACKING update (Geoff signs off on it at hand-back (c)).

## Design constraints

- **Stdlib only** (root module; `net/http`/`net/http/httptest` are fine). No network in tests — httptest exclusively.
- **CUE owns shape**: extend `kits/mcp-server/schema.cue` + testdata for the data-shaped `HTTPOptions` fields (`MaxBodyBytes`, `AllowedOrigins`); `RandHex` stays out of CUE (behavioral seam, `CallLog` precedent). `mcp-client` stays schema-less; `telemetry/event`'s existing `schema.cue` is untouched (the codec is behavioral, no new data shape).
- **Injected clocks/randomness**: reuse `Server.now`; new randomness only via the existing `randHex(nBytes int) string` seam (nil-default documented, per `trace.go`).
- **Org-agnostic**: no endpoint URLs, no product names, no protocol-version negotiation hardcoded beyond the existing `knownProtocolVersions` table; `AllowedOrigins` is caller-supplied config, never a baked-in host list.
- **Layering**: `telemetry/event` gains zero new imports beyond stdlib string handling — the codec is string-based on purpose so `event` never imports `net/http`; callers do `header.Set(event.TraceparentHeader, …)`. `bounded-exec` → `telemetry/event` is foundation→sibling-foundation (allowed). Kit imports both.
- **Concurrency contract** in every touched package doc: `NewHTTPHandler` is safe for concurrent requests (dispatch core is; call-log writer is mutex-guarded — but note stdio `Serve` is one-at-a-time while HTTP is concurrent: state this difference explicitly). `NewHTTPTransport` is NOT concurrency-safe standalone; `Client` serializes it (same contract as `ioTransport`).
- **Honest non-guarantees**: no TLS/auth (deferred per design note table), no session resumability, no SSE, notifications-to-client impossible in stateless mode, stdio carries no trace (design record's stated position). Origin validation IS provided (above) — it is the one HTTP-security MUST implemented now; keep the rest of the deferred table honest.
- Compose, don't duplicate: reuse `rpcRequest`/`rpcResponse`/`rpcError`, `bestEffortID`, `dispatch`, `serveReq`, `DefaultMaxMessageBytes`. The ONLY refactor to existing code is the `serveOne` extraction.

## Non-goals & theater traps

- **Do not build**: the deprecated HTTP+SSE two-connection transport (design note §"What this is not"); `mcp-session-id`/resumability; SSE streaming responses or progress notifications; prompts/resources capabilities (trigger unfired); OAuth/TLS; `tracestate`/OTLP/OTel semconv (roadmap #26); any change to sextant's `servehttp.go` (H4, read-only here); a second trace-context type — `event.TraceContext` is canonical.
- **Already exists — do not re-build**: message-size bounding + resync (`readLine`/`bestEffortID`), version negotiation (`handleInitialize`), tool pinning, `RegisterAll` bridge, call logging, harness trace rooting.
- Theater traps: (1) an HTTP handler that re-implements dispatch instead of extracting `serveOne` — the conformance test exists to make divergence fail, don't weaken it; (2) claiming "W3C compliant" while only handling version `00` happy-path — the parse tests must include future-version and all-zero-id cases; (3) marking #21 graduated while only the HTTP leg works — the env/bounded-exec canary is part of the claim; (4) bumping to a 2026 protocol version constant on RC rumor — the RC finalizes 2026-07-28, after this work; (5) `[x]` on any box before the gate run that includes it; (6) "passing" the notification conformance case by asserting only the 202 status — the empty-body assertion is the equivalence; (7) writing "not required" for MCP-Protocol-Version in prose without the three conformance cases backing it.
